items.title: Snip: the developer drags a rectangle over the editor and the agent receives the crop plus where they were
items.evidence: Asked for by the developer 2026-10-21. User problem: pointing at a visual problem means describing it in words; frequency: every visual review; saving: the agent gets the crop, map, camera, panel text and placements under the rectangle in one call; risk: a new gesture and a text field (register in editor::Fields), and snips are files in the project (confine and name them). Progress 2026-10-21 (556801e): the agent half shipped as emerge_snip { label, rect } (crop of a window-pixel rectangle, with path and state). Still open: the human drag gesture in the editor (UI state machine plus a registered operation that emits the snip). Iteration 2026-10-21-baseline-f7a8a9d did not take it: the human half needs (1) a note field registered in editor::Fields, (2) a windowed Screenshot crop inside bevy_emerge_mapper (the crop lives in bevy_emerge_mcp/src/snip.rs; move it to core rather than copy it), and (3) a decision whether a completed snip is a registry operation (it changes no map) or a documented gesture whose MCP front end is emerge_snip. Not a one-iteration slice without a reduction. Design settled 2026-10-21: a completed snip is a capture (like emerge_capture_still and emerge_snip), not a registry operation, since it changes no map state; the person's trigger is a new keys::Action plus a note field registered in editor::Fields, so it needs E-024 (one migration) first or in the same commit. Shipped in the 2026-10-22 snip iteration (a5b4dc0, branch loop/2026-10-22-snip): the person arms Cmd+\, drags a rectangle, types a note and presses Enter; the agent reads it with emerge_list_snips. Report docs/loop/iterations/2026-10-22-snip-a5b4dc0.md.

items.title: Migrate one unmigrated keys::Action into the operation registry, so an agent can do it and new human actions can be paid for
items.evidence: Unblocked by E-025's decision: Decided by the developer 2026-10-22: actions name their operation. A keys::Action counts as migrated when its binding dispatches a registered operation, checked mechanically (the action names its operation id; the parity test verifies the id against the registry and that the UI path dispatches it). The Typing guard stays, because the action stays in keys::Action. The parity test's definition of 'migrated' changes accordingly, and the allowlist keeps shrinking: lower UNMIGRATED_MAX by one per migrated action. First migration: placement_set_pin (O key, Action::OwnToggle); work in progress preserved at target/loop/wip/e024-pin-wip.patch and target/loop/wip/e024-an_agent_can_pin_a_placement.rs (3 agent tests that failed before and passed with the patch). operations_have_two_front_ends::the_allowlist_of_unmigrated_actions_only_shrinks pins UNMIGRATED_MAX = 128 and says a new non-operation action must be paid for by migrating one in the same commit. It is what blocked E-021 (Home frame key, 2026-10-21 frame iteration) and E-014's human half (2026-10-21 baseline iteration). User problem: an agent cannot perform the migrated verb today, and the person's next actions cannot land; frequency: every new human verb; saving: unblocks E-014 and E-021 and adds one agent verb; risk: the verb's undo must go through the registry like map_set_settings (see B-008's Undo::Settings). Pick a small map-changing verb with a clear inverse.
items.last_failure: 2026-10-21 pin iteration (base 74f5085): chose placement_set_pin (O key, Action::OwnToggle). The pin verb itself passed its 3 agent tests and the editor's pin, unpin and reason paths dispatched it. Blocked by operations_have_two_front_ends: the_allowlist_of_unmigrated_actions_only_shrinks asserts UNMIGRATED == Action::ALL (every keys::Action variant is listed), so removing OwnToggle from UNMIGRATED fails unless the variant leaves the enum. Leaving the enum means rebinding O outside keys::Action, which drops the Typing-field guard (a name typed with O would pin); or redesigning the keymap so bindings name operations. Either is a design decision, not one verb. WIP patch kept outside the repo at /tmp/e024-pin-wip.patch.

items.title: one_undo_takes_back_the_newest_change fails under load on Linux CI (load-dependent flake)

must_fix.evidence: Cycle 7 judgment 2 of 3: blocks no, common yes, no workaround yes (red CI on main line, not a user-facing defect).

items.root_cause: Undo of Undo::Added, Undo::Moved and the put-back path in editor.rs apply() changed open.map in memory and never wrote the file. The 250 ms file watcher then read the stale file as an outside edit and adopted it, putting the undone run back. Under CPU oversubscription the watcher's poll lands between the undo and the next save, which is why only loaded runs failed. Fix: apply() persists the map after each of those changes (a failed write goes to Status::problem). Regression test one_undo_takes_back_the_newest_change::cmd_z_on_a_run_writes_the_map_so_the_watcher_has_nothing_to_adopt fails before on macOS too ('Cmd+Z took the run back in memory, but the file still holds it') and passes after. Found by the C9Linux state trace on big.
items.evidence: crates/bevy_emerge_mapper/tests/one_undo_takes_back_the_newest_change.rs::cmd_z_after_a_resize_takes_back_the_resize_and_not_an_older_edit fails :138 (left 4, right 0) and :145 (left 8, right 4). CI red on ab5ebf8 (run 39926254825); green on f36ee00 (39906306802) and b99c056 (39935647016). Stress: f36ee00 44/120, ab5ebf8 67/320, single-process 0/300 (8 concurrent xvfb-run workers pinned to taskset -c 0,1). Ruled out: duplicate Undo/Redo handlers, Placement marker split, key-context race, time-based repeat. Suspect: apply for Undo::Added/Undo::Moved (editor.rs ~7726-7813) via undo()/redo(). Next: log undo_len/redo_len and placement count under stress. Evidence: local://c7-linux-notes.md (not in repo). Report: docs/loop/iterations/2026-10-23-cycle7-e89e86f.md
